one Base Residual Auction exception, and (ii) evidence of corporate commitment (e.g., an SEC
filing, a press release, or a letter from a duly authorized corporate officer indicating intent to
make such investment). Periodic updates on the progress, shall be provided by the Capacity
Market Seller to the Office of the Interconnection and the Market Monitoring Unit for their
 review by no later than (i) one hundred twenty (120) days prior to the commencement of the
offer period for subsequent Incremental Auctions for the applicable Delivery Years, and (ii) the
December 1 that last precedes subsequent Base Residual Auctions. The Capacity Market Seller
shall also immediately notify the Office of the Interconnection and the Market Monitoring Unit
of any material changes to the plan that may occur. Upon request by a Capacity Market Seller, a
one year extension to the plan timeline shall be permissible only for delays not caused by the
Capacity Market Seller, and that could not have been remedied through the exercise of due
diligence by the Capacity Market Seller. In no event may an exception be requested by the
Capacity Market Seller for more than two Base Residual Auctions.

         Failure to submit a documented plan, or lack of good faith effort by a Capacity Market
Seller to make an Existing Generation Capacity Resource physically capable of meeting the
requirements of a Capacity Performance Resource in accordance with a documented plan, shall
result in the removal of the resource’s Capacity Resource status effective with the first future
Delivery Year for which the resource was granted an exception, no earlier than the 2023/2024
Delivery Year. The Office of the Interconnection shall amend the applicable Interconnection
Service Agreement or wholesale market participation agreement to reflect any such removal of
the Capacity Interconnection Rights, and shall report the amended agreement to the Commission
in the same manner as the original (e.g. FERC Filing or Electronic Quarterly Reports). The
Office of the Interconnection shall file the amended agreement unexecuted if the Interconnection
Customer or wholesale market participant does not sign the amended Interconnection Service
Agreement or wholesale market participation agreement. The required change in Capacity
Resource status shall only apply to those Generation Capacity Resources that are shown to be
physically incapable of satisfying the requirements of a Capacity Performance Resource.

        (d)    A resource not exempted or excepted under subsection (c) hereof that is capable
of qualifying as a Capacity Performance Resource and does not offer into an RPM Auction as a
Capacity Performance Resource shall be subject to the same restrictions on subsequent offers,
and other possible remedies, as specified in section 6.6.

        (e)     An RBP Resource committed through the Reliability Backstop Procurement must
offer all committed RBP UCAP MW as price-takers (i.e., $0/MW-day) into the applicable RPM
Auctions pursuant to the capacity must offer requirements and exceptions set forth in Tariff,
Attachment DD, sections 6.6 and 6.6A. The applicable RPM Auctions shall be the Reliability
Pricing Model Auctions beginning with the first Delivery Year in which an RBP Resource has
been committed through the Reliability Backstop Procurement and is expected to be in-service.
Such offer requirement shall continue for each subsequent Delivery Year through the end of the
fixed 15-year term, except RBP UCAP MW for Capacity Performance Resources without a
notice of intent to offer submitted pursuant to Tariff, Attachment DD, section 5.5 for the
2030/2031 Base Residual Auction, which shall have a must offer requirement beginning in the
next applicable RPM Auction, including but not limited to the 2031/2032 Base Residual Auction
and the 2029/2030 Second Incremental Auction to the extent such resource has an RBP UCAP
MW commitment and is expected to be in-service for those Delivery Years.
 18.    RELIABILITY BACKSTOP PROCUREMENT

The Reliability Backstop Procurement or “RBP” is a one-time procurement, starting in 2027, to
address resource adequacy challenges in the PJM Region arising from insufficient capacity
committed through Reliability Pricing Model Auctions starting in the 2027/2028 Delivery Year.
 18.1   Determination of Final RBP Target

The Reliability Backstop Procurement is designed to procure sufficient RBP UCAP MW to meet
the Final RBP Target.

        (a)    Initial RBP Target
        The Initial RBP Target shall be a region-wide value equal to the lesser of the (1) most up
to date UCAP MW quantity that PJM cleared short of the PJM Region Reliability Requirement
for the 2028/2029 Delivery Year Base Residual Auction or (2) the UCAP equivalent of the
aggregate region-wide Large Load MW quantity reported by the Electric Distributor in accordance
with Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.3A. Specifically, the Initial RBP Target shall equal the
lesser of ([the latest estimate of the PJM Region Reliability Requirement for the 2028/2029
Delivery Year, calculated as the RTO Region Peak Load Forecast for the 2028/2029 Delivery Year
from the 2027 Load Forecast times the 2028/2029 Forecast Pool Requirement from the updated
planning parameters available at the commencement of the RBP, less the sum of all updated
Unforced Capacity Obligations of FRR Entities in the PJM Region] minus [the UCAP-equivalent
of the ICAP quantity of Capacity Resources that cleared in the 2028/2029 Base Residual Auction
using the latest capacity accreditation factors for the 2028/2029 Delivery Year available at the
commencement of the RBP], the aggregate region-wide Large Load MW reported by the Electric
Distributor in accordance with Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.3A times the most recent
2028/2029 Forecast Pool Requirement).

        (b)   Final RBP Target
The Final RBP Target shall be a PJM region-wide value equal to the Initial RBP Target minus the
total PJM region-wide Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW and the unforced capacity obligation
value of load that have successfully requested and obtained an opt-out pursuant to Tariff,
Attachment DD, section 18.1(d).

        (c)    Fixed Resource Requirement Entities
Fixed Resource Requirement (“FRR”) Entities as of the 2028/2029 Delivery Year shall be
excluded from the Reliability Backstop Procurement, including Initial and Final RBP Targets.
To the extent an Electric Distributor zone/area that has RBP UCAP MW committed through the
Reliability Backstop Procurement later becomes an FRR Service Area pursuant to RAA, Schedule
8.1.D, the Electric Distributor zone/area shall continue to be accountable for the RBP UCAP MW
quantity committed through the Reliability Backstop Procurement.

       (d)      Opt-Out
When calculating the Final RBP Target, the Initial RBP Target shall also be decremented, if
requested by an Electric Distributor, and accompanied by an officer attestation in accordance with
the PJM Manuals, by up to the associated MW quantity of load that participates in a peak shaving
adjustment program for a minimum period of five years where such Electric Distributor’s
zone/area addresses their capacity needs through peak shaving adjustment programs that are
codified in state law and that also meet the requirements of Tariff, Attachment DD-2.
 18.2   Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW

        (a)      Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW is capacity that will be located within the PJM
Region (i) has not previously supported a capacity commitment or been committed in an FRR Plan
for the 2028/2029 or earlier Delivery Year as of the commencement of the Reliability Backstop
Procurement (except for capacity that is first committed in the Third Incremental Auction
associated with the 2027/2028 Delivery Year); and (ii) is supplied by a resource that satisfies each
of the criteria set forth in Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.2(b).

       (b)     Resources Eligible to Supply Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW

A resource eligible to supply Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW must have an expected
commercial operation date, or is reasonably expected to be an Annual Demand Resource or DER
Capacity Aggregation Resource that will be registered with the Office of the Interconnection and
under a contract to perform based on PJM dispatch instructions, by no later than June 1, 2032 and
be: (i) a new build generation resource including new resources that obtain Capacity
Interconnection Rights transferred from deactivated resources or resources that have announced
deactivation as of April 10, 2026; (ii) the incremental capacity created by an uprate of existing
Generation Capacity Resources, but only to the extent such incremental capacity is created through
an increase in such Generation Capacity Resource’s installed capacity and increase in Capacity
Interconnection Rights associated with that Generation Capacity Resource; (iii) the incremental
capacity created by the utilization of Surplus Interconnection Service; (iv) repowering of a
deactivated generation resource that deactivated prior to April 10, 2026; (v) incremental capacity,
whether due to greater Unforced Capacity or a higher level of Capacity Interconnection Rights,
created by an existing Generation Capacity Resource’s changing fuel type to a more efficient fuel
type; or (vi) Planned Demand Resource or Planned DER Capacity Aggregation Resources, as
described in the RAA, Schedule 6 and Schedule 6.2 , and must meet the requirements of being
eligible to be an RBP Resource as set forth in Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.5(c) and 18.5(d),
except that the associated participation contract(s) are not required to be eligible for the offset.
.

       (c)     Evidence of Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW

During the RBP bid submission window defined in Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.4, Electric
Distributors shall report the Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW that is the subject of a bilateral
agreement with a Large Load, up to the capacity obligation of the Large Load, reported to the
Office of the Interconnection in accordance with Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.3(a)(2) in their
respective zones/areas. Such report shall be accompanied by evidence of at least one of the
following supporting materials. Likewise, to the extent LSEs, interconnecting customers, large
loads, Transmission Owners, or other entities report Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW to the
Office of the Interconnection during such RBP bid submission window, the reported Qualifying
RBP Offset UCAP MW must be accompanied with evidence of at least one of the following
supporting materials:

              (i)    Signed bilateral contracts for Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW for at least
       five Delivery Years with a commercial operation date prior to the start of the 2032/2033
        Delivery Year, and matched with Large Load that has an executed electric service
       agreement or transmission service agreement, indicating that the load will be coming online
       in the 2027/2028 or 2028/2029 Delivery Year;

               (ii)   Self-Supply generation that is in a Relevant Electric Retail Regulatory
       Authority (“RERRA”)-approved or accepted integrated resource plan with either
       associated generation in the PJM interconnection queue or signed bilateral contracts for
       Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW for at least five Delivery Years with a commercial
       operation date prior to the start of the 2032/2033 Delivery Year, and matched with load
       that has an executed electric service agreement or transmission service agreement,
       indicating that the Large Load will be coming online in the 2027/2028 or 2028/2029
       Delivery Year; or

               (iii) Signed commitment between a Curtailment Service Provider or DER
       Aggregator and new load(s) that has an executed electric service agreement or transmission
       service agreement, indicating that the new Large Load(s) will, in a MW quantity equal to
       MW quantity of the new load(s), either (a) participate as Annual Demand Resources or
       DER Capacity Aggregation Resources starting in the 2028/2029 Delivery Year Second
       Incremental Auction and continuing through the 2032/2033 Delivery Year, or (b) purchase
       replacement Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW that are eligible generation or storage
       resources.

        (d)    To determine the quantity of any Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW that are
verified by the Office of the Interconnection and used to decrement the Initial RBP Target, the
Office of the Interconnection shall use the most up-to-date ELCC Class Ratings associated with
the 2028/2029 Delivery Year, or the estimated unit-specific UCAP value for resources with no
ELCC Class Rating available at the commencement of the RBP.

        (e)     The total quantity of Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW verified by the Office of
the Interconnection and used to decrement the Initial RBP Target total amount allowed for each
zone/area will be capped by the aggregate MW quantity of Large Load reported by each Electric
Distributor, as reported in accordance with Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.3(a)(2), and the total
MW quantity that is subject to the RBP opt-out, as requested in accordance with Tariff, Attachment
DD, section 18.1(d), for the relevant zone/area.
 18.3    Allocation of RBP Charges, Credits, and Shortfall Charges

       (a)     Allocation of RBP Charges to Electric Distributor zone/area

(i) The Office of the Interconnection shall allocate the Initial RBP Target MW to each Electric
Distributor’s zone/area using that zone/area’s pro-rata share of the total incremental Large Load
reported to the Office of the Interconnection in accordance with Tariff, Attachment DD, section
18.3A. Such allocation shall be only to Electric Distributors’ zone/area not located in an FRR
Service Area and based on information provided by each such Electric Distributor.



(ii) The allocation based on the zone/area’s MW share of the total incremental Large Load MW
shall be reduced for the purpose of this calculation to the extent:

              (1)     an Electric Distributor, LSE, Transmission Owner, or other entity provides
       the Office of Interconnection with evidence of Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW, in
       accordance with Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.2 and as may be further set forth in the
       PJM Manuals; or

              (2)    an Electric Distributor zone/area meets the opt-out provisions set forth in
       accordance with Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.1(d).

The resulting reduced MW, floored at zero, shall be used to calculate the zone/area’s assigned pro-
rata share of the Final RBP Target MW. The zone/area’s assigned share of the Final RBP Target
MW shall remain constant throughout the fixed, 15-year term.

(iii) The Office of the Interconnection shall allocate the total RBP Charges, assessed daily, to an
Electric Distributor’s zone/area on a pro-rata basis using the zone/area’s assigned share of the total
Final RBP Target MW across all zone/areas.

       (b)     Allocation of RBP Charges to Load Serving Entities

        LSEs located in an Electric Distributor zone/area with a positive, non-zero allocation of
RBP Charges pursuant to Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.3(a)(iii) shall be eligible to be
allocated responsibility for RBP Charges as follows:

              (i)     The daily assessed RBP Charges allocated to each Electric Distributor
       zone/area shall be further allocated to each applicable LSE within that zone/area with an
       RBP Obligation (“RBO”) based on the LSE’s pro-rata share of the total RBP Obligation
       MW for the zone/area.

               (ii)   The RBP Charge assessed daily to an LSE in a zone/area shall be the LSE’s
       daily reported RBO MW in the zone/area divided by the total RBO MW in the zone/area
       multiplied by total, daily RBP Charges allocated to the zone/area.
         (iii)  The RBO MW shall be, where available, the state and/or RERRA-
determined allocation of cleared RBP UCAP MW to LSEs within each Electric
Distributor’s zone/area, as reported by each Electric Distributor to the Office of the
Interconnection, with the initial allocation reported no later than one hundred and twenty
(120) days prior to the 2028/2029 Delivery Year. Electric Distributors may report updated
RBO MW to the Office of the Interconnection after the initial allocation is reported to
reflect any changes in Load Serving Entities that should be assigned RBP Charges. If no
RBO MW are reported to the Office of the Interconnection for an Electric Distributor
zone/area, PJM will allocate the RBP Charges for that zone/area to all load in the zone/area
using each LSE’s ratio share of the Daily Unforced Capacity Obligation for the zone/area
as determined in RAA, Schedule 8. PJMSettlement shall be the Counterparty to each LSE’s
obligation to pay, and payments of, RBP Charges.

       (iv)    RBP Shortfall Charges will be allocated to LSEs as credits based on using
the same pro-rata share of the RBP Charges, pursuant to RAA, Article 7, section 7.2B.
 18.3A Electric Distributor Reporting Requirement for Reliability Backstop Procurement

No later than seven days prior to the commencement of the Reliability Backstop Procurement, each
Electric Distributor outside of an FRR Service Area shall report to the Office of the Interconnection
the quantity and identity of incremental Large Load that is supported by an electric service
obligation, construction commitment, or similar agreement. Such Electric Distributor shall also
report the amount (in MW) that represents the difference between the aggregate quantity of Large
Load based on the 2026 actual summer peak and the expected summer peak of Large Load for the
2028/2029 Delivery Year. An Electric Distributor shall provide an explanation for any deviation
between the expected quantity of Large Loads for the 2028/2029 Delivery Year and the values
provided by the Electric Distributor to the Office of the Interconnection as part of the development
for the load forecast.
 18.4   Scope of the Reliability Backstop Procurement

The Office of the Interconnection shall conduct an RBP to commit RBP Resources up to the UCAP
MW value to meet the Final RBP Target. The Reliability Backstop Procurement offer submission
window for RBP Sell Offers shall open for four weeks. The clearing and selection process will
take place thereafter and concluding six weeks following the close of the offer submission window.
The Office of the Interconnection shall notify RBP Sellers that receive a commitment as an RBP
Resource as soon as practicable upon the conclusion of the RBP. The Office of the Interconnection
shall post specific dates on the PJM website prior to the commencement of the Reliability Backstop
Procurement.

RBP Sellers may submit RBP Sell Offers of RBP Resources supporting RBP UCAP MW into the
Reliability Backstop Procurement. PJMSettlement shall be the Counterparty to the transactions
arising from the RBP.

An RBP Sell Offer will be considered binding once any PJM-identified deficiencies are cured and
until the conclusion of the Reliability Backstop Procurement and the underlying resource does not
receive a commitment in the Reliability Backstop Procurement.

The Reliability Backstop Procurement shall offer commitments for RBP UCAP MW for a fixed
period of fifteen (15) Delivery Years, starting with the 2028/2029 Delivery Year. Resources with
a commercial operation date later than the 2028/2029 Delivery Year shall be committed for the
remainder of the fifteen-year term of the Reliability Backstop Procurement commitment period,
i.e. through the end of the 2042/2043 Delivery Year.
 18.5   The Reliability Backstop Procurement Process

      (a)    RBP Seller Eligibility to Participate and General Requirements for Resources
Supporting RBP UCAP MW

To be eligible to participate in the Reliability Backstop Procurement, an RBP Seller must meet the
RBP credit requirements, set forth in Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.8, with RBP Sell Offer(s)
for RBP UCAP MW based on a resource that:

               (i)     Has a commercial operation date, or is reasonably expected to be an Annual
       Demand Resource or DER Capacity Aggregation Resource that will be registered with the
       Office of the Interconnection and under a contract to perform based on PJM dispatch
       instructions, by no later than June 1, 2032, inclusive of any required Network Upgrades;

               (ii)  Has not received a capacity commitment or been committed in an FRR Plan
       for the 2028/2029 or earlier Delivery Year as of the commencement of the Reliability
       Backstop Procurement (except for capacity that is first committed in the Third Incremental
       Auction associated with the 2027/2028 Delivery Year);

               (iii)   Is not supplying Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW;

              (iv)   To the extent the subject of a notice of intent for the 2028/2029 Base
       Residual Auction, must have offered and not cleared in the 2028/2029 Base Residual
       Auction; and

               (v)     Meets the requirements in Tariff, Attachment DD, sections 18.5(b), 18.5(c),
       or 18.5(d).

       (b)     Generation or Energy Storage Resources as an RBP Resource

To qualify as an RBP Resource, a generation or Energy Storage Resource that supplies RBP UCAP
MW eligible to be offered into the Reliability Backstop Procurement shall be in the PJM Region
or meet the requirements to pseudo-tie into the PJM Region in Tariff, Attachment DD, section
5.5A(b), must meet the requirements of Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.5(a) and must be:

               (i)     Composed of new Installed Capacity and new Maximum Facility Output;

              (ii)    Supported by new Capacity Interconnection Rights (if located in the PJM
       Region) or Capacity Interconnection Rights transferred from a deactivated resource or a
       resource that announced deactivation as of April 10, 2026; and

              (iii)   Consist of (1) new build; (2) incremental capacity created by an uprate of
       an existing Generation Capacity Resource’s or Energy Storage Resource’s installed
       capacity and associated level of Capacity Interconnection Rights; or (3) repowering of a
       generation resource that had deactivated, or announced deactivation, on or before April 10,
       2026.
        (c)    RBP Demand Resources

To qualify as a Demand Resource that supplies RBP UCAP MW eligible to be offered into the
Reliability Backstop Procurement, a Demand Resource must meet the requirements of Tariff,
Attachment DD, sections 18.5(a), and:

              (i)     Not be reliant on or composed of registered location(s) that previously
       supported a Demand Resource that provided capacity in the 2026/2027 Delivery Year
       unless such location represents an incremental increase in capacity resulting from an
       investment in new generation or new storage resources at that location; and

               (ii)    Identify, as part of its RBP Sell Offer, for the full length of the fixed term,
       the location(s) and associated participation contract(s).

       (d)    RBP DER Aggregation Resources

To qualify as a DER Capacity Aggregation Resource that supplies RBP UCAP MW eligible to be
offered into the Reliability Backstop Procurement, a Planned DER Capacity Aggregation Resource
must meet the requirements of Tariff, Attachment DD, sections 18.5(a) and:

               (i)    Identify, as part of its RBP Sell Offer, for the length of the fixed term, the
       location(s) and associated participation contract(s).

       (e)    RBP Sell Offers

RBP Sell Offers for RBP UCAP MW shall specify an offer quantity in UCAP MW and an offer
price in $/MW-day UCAP for each Delivery Year beginning with the first full Delivery Year in
which the RBP UCAP MW is expected to provide capacity through the end of the fixed 15-year
term.

RBP Sellers will be responsible for all actual Network Upgrade costs as determined through the
interconnection process, without subsequent adjustments to RBP Sell Offers.

Each RBP Sell Offer shall include the following information for the RBP UCAP MW offered:

              (i)     the MW of UCAP to be provided by such resource for each Delivery Year,
       where the maximum UCAP included in an RBP Sell Offer shall be limited to no greater
       than 120% of the resource type’s most recent maximum Preliminary ELCC Class Ratings
       for 2028/2029 through the last posted Delivery Year or based on the resource’s maximum
       estimated unit-specific ELCC ratings across such period for resources with no ELCC Class
       Rating, multiplied by the resource’s ICAP;

                (ii)   the price in $/MW-day UCAP for each Delivery Year beginning with the
       first full Delivery Year in which the RBP UCAP MW is expected to provide capacity
       through the end of the fixed 15-year term;
                (iii)  the first full Delivery Year for which such resource shall be available and
       offering to provide capacity;

               (iv)   all relevant documentation necessary for the Office of the Interconnection
       to evaluate whether the project satisfies the gating criteria, as set forth in Tariff, Attachment
       DD, section 18.5(f)(i).

       (f)     Clearing Structure

Following the closing date of bid solicitation for the Reliability Backstop Procurement, the Office
of the Interconnection shall complete the Reliability Backstop Procurement in two stages: (1)
gating criteria evaluation and (2) selection assessment, with notification of finalized commitments
posted prior to the Base Residual Auction for the 2030/2031 Delivery Year. The Reliability
Backstop Procurement shall be pay-as-bid.

               (i)     Stage 1: Gating Criteria Evaluation

       A valid RBP Sell Offer shall include the information and evidence required by this section.
       The Office of the Interconnection shall evaluate all RBP Sell Offers for compliance with
       this requirement. Such evaluation shall be conducted by the Office of the Interconnection
       on a pass/fail basis.

       RBP Sell Offers that do not include the following information shall not proceed to selection
       assessment, provided, however, that the Office of the Interconnection shall provide the
       RBP Seller the opportunity to cure any identified deficiencies within five (5) calendar days
       of being notified by PJM.

      RBP Sell Offers for RBP Generation and/or Storage Capacity Resources must be
accompanied by:

                      (1)      A critical path construction schedule and expected commercial
               operation date, with attestation, for the Office of the Interconnection to validate that
               RBP Sell Offers are for RBP UCAP MW with a feasible commercial operation date
               of June 1, 2032 or earlier;

                              (A)     With respect to a project in Transition Cycle #2 under Tariff,
                       Part VII and earlier, such project must provide study information and
                       timeline from its most current PJM study;

                               (B)    With respect to a project in Cycle 1 under Tariff Part VIII,
                       the Expedited Interconnection Track under Tariff, Part X, or not under
                       study, the project must provide study information and timeline from (1) an
                       independent consultant report or (2) the most current PJM study;
         (2)      For projects that are not the subject of a completed interconnection
study or are not currently under study as part of an active New Service Request by
the Office of the Interconnection, evidence of 100% Site Control consistent with
Tariff, Part VIII, Subpart A, section 402 for each of the Generating Facility
(including the location of the main step-up transformer), the Interconnection
Facilities, and the Interconnection Switchyard (as defined in the PJM Manuals) for
a term of at least three years from the date of submission of the RBP Sell Offer.

         Such projects must also be accompanied by a certification, executed by an
officer or authorized representative of the Generation Project Developer, verifying
that the Site Control requirements have been met. Further, at Transmission
Provider’s request, Generation Project Developer shall provide copies of landowner
attestations or county recordings. The Site Control requirements include an acreage
requirement for the Project, as set forth in the PJM Manuals.


        (3)    Financing plan, i.e., identified financing sources and details (e.g.,
project financing, balance sheets, tax equity, sponsor equity), current status of any
financing commitments or term sheets, and a general description of the capital
structure and expected timeline to financial close;

       (4)     Permitting plan, e.g., a list of all applicable permits, current status,
and timeline to obtain each;

       (5)     Signed memorandum for the acquisition of major equipment,
invoices or agreements to acquire major equipment, or other documentary evidence
that major equipment has been procured;

        (6)    Evidence of experience having constructed a previous project of
similar size and technology or have contracted with an engineering, procurement,
and construction partner with such experience, or contract with an engineering,
procurement, and construction partner with such experience;

        (7)     For natural gas-fueled generation resources, evidence of delivery
infrastructure arrangements in the form of a notice of intent or attestation of pipeline
capacity expansion to support the new project; and

         (8)     For generation and/or energy storage resources located outside of
the PJM Region, evidence of (a) a completed facilities study or equivalent under
the host Regional Transmission Organization/Independent System Operator’s or
utility’s interconnection process and (b) long-term firm point-to-point transmission
service, or a confirmed transmission service request with a completed system
impact study, sufficient to deliver capacity to the border of the PJM Region
consistent with the requirements of Tariff, Attachment DD, section 5.5A(b).
 RBP Sell Offers for Demand Resources or DER Capacity Aggregation Resources must be
accompanied by:

              (9)    Locations within the PJM Region by Zone/Sub-zonal LDA and
       aggregate capacity for RBP Sell Offers;

              (10) Executed customer agreements or binding commitments covering
       the proposed RBP UCAP MW commitment, with identified locations, customer
       names, and expected curtailment/injection capability per site; and

               (11) Equipment procurement plan or evidence of deployed enabling
       infrastructure such as metering, telemetry, load control, SCADA/dispatch systems,
       or DER major equipment as applicable.

RBP Sell Offers for DER Capacity Aggregation Resources must also be accompanied by:

               (12) Applicable Electric Distributor interconnection/distribution impact
       study requirements and a plan to initiate on a timeline consistent with the proposed
       delivery date.

RBP Sell Offers for Demand Resources must also be accompanied by:

              (13) Electric Distributor coordination requirements for metering,
       telemetry, and baseline measurement infrastructure.

       (ii)    Stage 2: Selection Assessment

All RBP Sell Offers that pass the gating criteria evaluation shall be evaluated based on the
first Delivery Year offered in the RBP Sell Offer, levelized cost, and RBP UCAP MW
quantity.

RBP Sell Offers shall be selected in rank order from earliest to latest offered Delivery Year,
and then in least-cost order based on the levelized cost ($/MW-day) of UCAP MW over
the fixed 15-year term, until the Final RBP Target is satisfied for any Delivery Year up
through the 2032/2033 Delivery Year. RBP Resources shall not be partially cleared. In
selecting the least-cost solution that satisfies the Final RBP Target and the cost of
procurement constraint, the Office of the Interconnection may commit an RBP Sell Offer
with an offered quantity that exceeds the remaining Final RBP Target to the extent such
solution provides greater economic efficiency than an alternative solution that satisfies the
requirements and constraints.

The levelized cost of each RBP Sell Offer shall be calculated as:

Levelized Cost ($/MW-day) = Net Present Value (RBP Sell Offer price x UCAP
offered)/Net Present Value (UCAP offered)
 with a discount rate equal to 9.5% after-tax average weighted average cost of capital
(ATWACC).

The MW-weighted average of the levelized procurement cost of all selected RBP Sell
Offers shall not exceed $555/MW-day UCAP.

In the event that two or more RBP Sell Offers with the same initial offered Delivery Year
and levelized cost, and fewer than all of such offers are needed to satisfy the Final RBP
Target, the Office of the Interconnection shall select the RBP Sell Offer(s) proposing
resources based on the earliest timestamp of such RBP Sell Offer(s).

In the event that the Reliability Backstop Procurement cannot meet the Final RBP Target,
the Reliability Backstop Procurement shall clear short of the Final RBP Target.

(g)    Settlement Structure

       (i)     UCAP MW Eligible to Be Settled as Contract for Difference

Each RBP Resource that has been committed in the Reliability Backstop Procurement shall
be individually settled as a contract for difference (“CfD”).

An RBP Resource’s total daily MW eligible to be settled as a CfD shall be the lesser of the
RBP Resource’s daily committed RBP UCAP MW, daily owned UCAP MW, and daily
cleared RPM UCAP MW.

All UCAP MW of an RBP Resource above the committed RBP UCAP MW shall be
eligible to participate in RPM Auctions, subject to existing RPM rules, without being
subject to RBP obligations or settlement.

       (ii)    RBP Settlement Credits Based on Contract for Difference

An RBP Resource’s contract for difference (“CfD”), represented as positive or negative
RBP Settlement Credits, shall be settled daily as the product of the total daily UCAP MW
eligible to settle as CfD and the difference between the price at which the RBP Resource
was committed in the Reliability Backstop Procurement for a Delivery Year and the RBP
Resource’s unit-specific weighted average resource clearing price of all applicable RPM
Auctions from the associated Delivery Year. Applicable RPM Auctions include all RPM
Auctions for the associated Delivery Year that are conducted after the Reliability Backstop
Procurement. If the RBP Resource is committed through the RBP for a Delivery Year in
which PJM has already conducted the Base Residual Auction, the CfD will be settled using
the difference between the price at which the RBP Resource was committed in the
Reliability Backstop Procurement for such Delivery Year and the weighted average
resource clearing price in the applicable Incremental Auction(s) for such Delivery Year.

       (iii)   RBP Charges
 RBP Charges shall be based on the total RBP Settlement Credits, positive and negative, of
all RBP Resources across the PJM Region.

RBP Charges shall be calculated daily and allocated to Load Serving Entities by the
relevant Electric Distributor(s) in accordance with Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.3(b)
and the RAA, Article 7, section 2B.
 18.6   RBP Resource Obligations

       (a)     Capacity Must Offer Obligation

An RBP Resource committed through the Reliability Backstop Procurement must offer all
committed RBP UCAP MW into the RPM Auctions as Capacity Resources pursuant to the
capacity must offer requirements and exceptions set forth in Tariff, Attachment DD, sections 6.6
and 6.6A. The applicable RPM Auctions shall be the Base Residual Auctions and Incremental
Auctions conducted after an RBP Resource’s RBP UCAP MW have been committed through the
Reliability Backstop Procurement beginning with the first Delivery Year in which such resource
is has an RBP commitment and is expected to be in service. Such offer requirement shall continue
for each subsequent Delivery Year through the end of the RBP term, except RBP UCAP MW for
RBP Resources that is expected to be in service for the 2030/2031 Delivery Year without a notice
of intent to offer submitted pursuant to Tariff, Attachment DD, section 5.5 for the 2030/2031 Base
Residual Auction shall have a must offer requirement in the next RPM Auction, including but not
limited to the 2031/2032 Base Residual Auction and the 2030/2031 First Incremental Auction.
The RBP Resource’s capacity must offer obligation into RPM Auctions for a Delivery Year is
satisfied once the entirety of the committed RBP UCAP MW have cleared in RPM Auction(s) for
such Delivery Year.

RBP Resources with RBP UCAP MW committed through RPM Auctions will be subject to all
RPM capacity market rules, as set forth in Tariff, Attachments DD and DD-1.

               (i)     Price

       RBP UCAP MW committed through the Reliability Backstop Procurement, and not
       qualifying for an exception pursuant to Tariff, Attachment DD, section 6.6(g), must be
       offered into the applicable RPM Auctions as price takers, i.e., $0/MW-day UCAP.

               (ii)    Quantity

       RBP Resources committed through the Reliability Backstop Procurement must be offered
       into the applicable RPM Auctions. The UCAP MW quantity offered in an applicable RPM
       Auction for the Delivery Year must be a quantity equal to the lesser of committed RBP
       UCAP MW minus total RPM committed MW through RPM Auctions for the Delivery
       Year and the available UCAP MW at the time of the RPM Auction.

       (b)     Exceptions to the Must Offer Obligation

An RBP Resource that is granted an exception to the RPM must-offer obligation, as set forth in
Tariff, Attachment DD, section 6.6(g) or 6.6A(c), shall nevertheless be subject to the RBP shortfall
charge.

       (c)     RBP Shortfall UCAP MW
 RBP UCAP MW committed through the Reliability Backstop Procurement that is unable to be
delivered in a Delivery Year within the fixed, 15-year period will not be compensated for the
undelivered megawatts via RBP Settlement Credits for each day the daily unforced capacity value
of the RBP Resource is below the daily committed RBP UCAP MW and will be subject to any
applicable RBP shortfall charges.

       (d)    RBP Shortfall Charges

RBP Resources with RBP UCAP MW committed through the Reliability Backstop Procurement
that are unable to meet its full RBP UCAP MW commitment due to not achieving commercial
operation by the first Delivery Year of the RBP commitment shall be subject to RBP shortfall
charges for the committed RBP UCAP MW until the resources achieves commercial operation,
for up to three years.

RBP shortfall charges shall be assessed daily, beginning in the first Delivery Year of the RBP
commitment, on the full RBP committed UCAP.

The RBP shortfall charge shall equal the committed RBP UCAP MW times a charge rate equal to
20% of the RBP commitment price of such resource (i.e., RBP shortfall charge = committed RBP
UCAP MW * 20% of RBP commitment price), for the applicable Delivery Year

              (i)    Exception to RBP Shortfall Charges

       An RBP Resource that is a generation or Energy Storage Resource and is unable to meet
       expected commercial operation date solely due to Network Upgrades shall be excepted
       from RBP shortfall charges if the RBP Resource successfully demonstrates readiness
       through test energy and seeks interim deliverability.

       (e)    Failure of RBP UCAP MW to Materialize

Commitments of RBP UCAP MW through the Reliability Backstop Procurement shall be
rescinded for the remainder of the fifteen-year term where RBP UCAP MW fail to come online
for three Delivery Years beginning with the first Delivery Year in which the RBP Resource was
committed. Once rescinded, RBP UCAP MW commitments will not be eligible to be compensated
as RBP UCAP MW for the remainder of the fixed 15-year term and shall no longer be subject to
RBP shortfall charges.

       (f)    Change in Ownership

Commitments of RBP UCAP MW shall follow the RBP Resource. With change in ownership of
the RBP Resource, the commitment of RBP UCAP MW shall be conveyed to the new owner and
continue through the end of the fixed 15-year term.
 18.7   Exiting Load Serving Entity RBP Obligations


In the event a Load Serving Entity that is allocated RBP Charges withdraws from PJM (whether
or not caused by the physical withdrawal of another entity from the PJM Region), such Load
Serving Entity shall be responsible for the remainder of the RBP Charges allocated to it, subject
to a rate filing with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission that details the specific terms and
amounts owed. Nothing in this provision shall limit such Load Serving Entity’s ability to seek
redress from another entity to the extent the Load Serving Entity’s withdrawal is caused by that
other entity’s physical withdrawal from the PJM Region.
 18.8 Credit Requirements for RBP Sellers and LSEs Allocated RBP Charges

The provisions of Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.8(a) shall apply to RBP Sellers seeking to
submit RBP Sell Offers in the Reliability Backstop Procurement. The provisions of Tariff,
Attachment DD, section 18.8(b) shall apply to LSEs allocated costs for RBP UCAP MW procured
through the Reliability Backstop Procurement, as determined in accordance with Tariff,
Attachment DD, section 18.3.

Settlement during any Delivery Year of cleared positions resulting from, or expected to result
from, the Reliability Backstop Procurement, including payments and Locational Reliability
Charges associated with the capacity commitments of RBP Resources, shall not be considered in
Peak Market Activity pursuant to Tariff, Attachment Q, Section VII.A. The forms of acceptable
credit support shall be limited to RBP Collateral.

The Reliability Backstop Procurement credit requirements described herein shall be separate from
and additional to any credit requirements for participation in RPM Auctions and bilateral
transactions under Tariff, Attachment DD, section 4.6, and other market activity in the PJM
Markets, as set forth in Tariff, Attachment Q, and shall be applied separately to each RBP Seller
with RBP Sell Offer and each LSE allocated cost for RBP UCAP MW procured through the
Reliability Backstop Procurement, as determined in accordance with Tariff, Attachment DD,
section 18.3.

       (a)    RBP Credit Requirements of RBP Sellers Seeking to Submit RBP Sell Offers

Prior to or simultaneous with submitting RBP Sell Offers, RBP Sellers seeking to participate in
the Reliability Backstop Procurement must post the appropriate amount of the RBP credit
requirement to each RBP Resource for which RBP Sell Offers are submitted.

              (i)     Applicability

       An RBP Seller seeking to submit an RBP Sell Offer in the Reliability Backstop
       Procurement must satisfy the credit requirement, i.e., the RBP credit requirement specified
       herein, prior to or simultaneously with submitting such RBP Sell Offer.

              (ii)    RBP Resource Credit Requirement

       The credit requirement applicable to an RBP Seller seeking to submit an RBP Sell Offer in
       the Reliability Backstop Procurement shall be the RBP credit requirement as provided in
       Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.8(iv).

       The total RBP credit requirement for each RBP Seller shall be, for the sum of the credit
       requirements for all RBP Sell Offers submitted by such RBP Seller in the Reliability
       Backstop Procurement.

              (iii)   Reduction in RBP Credit Requirement
                        (A)     The RBP credit requirement shall be returned for any RBP
                Resources that do not receive a commitment through the Reliability Backstop
                Procurement, within five (5) business days of the completion of the clearing process
                pursuant to Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.5(f).

                       (B)     Where an RBP Seller’s RBP Sell Offer is committed through the
                Reliability Backstop Procurement and the RBP Resource subsequently achieves
                commercial operation, the Office of the Interconnection may return the RBP credit
                requirement after a one-year look-back from the achievement of commercial
                operation.

             (iv)    Calculation of RBP Credit Requirement for RBP Sellers Seeking to submit
       RBP Sell Offers in the RBP

       RBP Sell Offers submitted by RBP Sellers in the Reliability Backstop Procurement shall
       be accompanied by a Reliability Backstop Procurement credit requirement, which shall be
       equal to:
          3
                                                     $
               0.2 × (𝑅𝐵𝑃 𝑆𝑒𝑙𝑙 𝑂𝑓𝑓𝑒𝑟 𝑃𝑟𝑖𝑐𝑒 𝑖𝑛          ) × (𝑈𝐶𝐴𝑃 𝑖𝑛 𝑀𝑊)𝑛 × 365
         𝑛=1                                  𝑀𝑊𝑑𝑎𝑦 𝑛
                                    𝑤ℎ𝑒𝑟𝑒 𝑛 = 𝐷𝑒𝑙𝑖𝑣𝑒𝑟𝑦 𝑌𝑒𝑎𝑟

                (v)    Credit Responsibility for Traded RBP Resource Commitment

       The Office of the Interconnection may require that credit and financial responsibility for a
       committed RBP Resource that is traded remain with the original party (which for these
       purposes, means the party bearing credit responsibility for the committed RBP Resource
       immediately prior to trade) unless the Office of the Interconnection determines that the
       receiving party has independently posted sufficient credit support with the Office of the
       Interconnection and agreed by providing written confirmation to the Office of the
       Interconnection that it will fully assume the credit responsibility associated with the
       committed RBP Resource. In determining the appropriate level of credit for any receiving
       party, the Office of the Interconnection may rely on Tariff, Attachment Q.

     (b)    RBP Credit Requirements Applicable to Load Serving Entities Responsible for
RBP Charges

Prior to the first Delivery Year, the assessment of an RBP credit requirement by the Office of the
Interconnection, LSEs allocated cost responsibility for RBP Charges, pursuant to Tariff,
Attachment DD, section 18.3, must post RBP Collateral for the RBP credit requirement, calculated
as set forth herein:

(i)    RBP Credit Requirement for Load Serving Entities
         (A)      The cumulative RBP credit requirement for Load Serving Entities for a
given Delivery Year shall be equivalent to RBP Credit Rate (as determined in accordance
with Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.8(b)(i)(B)) multiplied by the committed RBP
UCAP MW amount, where the committed RBP UCAP MW amount shall equal the total
amount of RBP UCAP MW that receives a commitment through the Reliability Backstop
Procurement and is supported by an RBP Resource that has reached commercial operation
by the start of the applicable Delivery Year. The foregoing determination of the committed
RBP UCAP MW amount shall exclude each commitment of RBP UCAP MW that is
rescinded pursuant to Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.6(e).

Following the commencement of commercial operation of all Capacity Resources with
RBP commitments, PJM shall review the RBP Credit Rate and present any
recommendations to stakeholders through the Members Committee.


When total posted RBP Collateral is greater than the total remaining RBP payment
obligations, the Office of the Interconnection will make available excess collateral, upon
request by an applicable Load Serving Entity.


        The cumulative RBP credit requirement for Load Serving Entities shall be met
through RBP Collateral posted by those Load Serving Entities allocated cost pursuant to
Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.3.

              (B)     The Office of the Interconnection shall apply the following credit
       requirements to each Load Serving Entity allocated responsibility for RBP
       Obligations, pursuant to Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.3, and each such LSE
       shall maintain credit support in an amount equal to its RBP LSE Credit
       Requirement, calculated as follows:

               RBP LSE Credit Requirement = RBP Credit Rate x Allocated RBP Credit
       MW

               For purposes of this calculation:

              RBP Credit Rate shall mean an amount per MW equal to 40% of the
       discounted total RBP payment obligation per MW over the applicable RBP
       commitment term, calculated using the weighted-average RBP clearing price of all
       RBP UCAP MW committed through the RBP.

              Allocated RBP Credit MW shall mean the amount of RBP UCAP MW,
       expressed in MW, for which the LSE has been allocated responsibility for RBP
       Charges in accordance with Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.3 and as determined
       in accordance with this Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.8(b)(i)(B)(1) or (2), as
       appropriate.
 (1)     For Load Serving Entities with an RBP Obligation in accordance Tariff,
Attachment DD, section 18.3, prior to forty-five (45) days before the start of a
given Delivery Year, such Load Serving Entities, must post, or maintain an
existing, RBP Collateral equal to the RBP Credit Rate multiplied by the Allocated
RBP Credit MW, where the zone/area allocated amount committed RBP UCAP
MW is further allocated to each Load Serving Entity based on the relevant Load
Serving Entity’s percent share of the zone/area’s RBP Obligation MW assigned
by the Electric Distributor. For Load Serving Entities required to post RBP
Collateral by this section 18.8(b)(i)(B)(1), the Office of the Interconnection may
evaluate such Load Serving Entity for unreasonable credit risk under the
Unreasonable Credit Risk provisions of Tariff, Attachment Q, Section II, and
require additional RBP Collateral as appropriate.


               (2)     To the extent such Load Serving Entity is allocated cost
       pursuant to Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.3 and no RBP Obligations
       are reported to the Office of the Interconnection in an Electric Distributor
       zone/area in which the Load Serving Entity serves load, prior to forty-five
       (45) days before the start of a given Delivery Year, such Load Serving
       Entities, may be required to post, or maintain an existing, RBP Collateral
       equal to the RBP Credit Rate multiplied by the allocated RBP Credit MW,
       where the zone/area committed RBP UCAP MW is allocated using the
       relevant Load Serving Entity’s proportional share of the Daily Unforced
       Capacity Obligation for the zone/area as determined in accordance with
       RAA, Schedule 8. For Load Serving Entities required to post RBP
       Collateral by this section 18.8(b)(i)(B)(2), the Office of the Interconnection
       may evaluate whether such Load Serving Entity for unreasonable credit risk
       under the Unreasonable Credit Risk provisions of Tariff, Attachment Q,
       Section II, and require additional RBP Collateral as appropriate.

       (C)    Credit Requirements Associated With Intra-Delivery Year Transfer
of Load and Allocated RBP UCAP MW Cost Responsibility

               (1)    To the extent a Load Serving Entity transfers its load serving
       obligations that are associated with committed RBP UCAP MW, as
       determined pursuant to Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.3, then the
       transferee LSE must fully satisfy all applicable credit and collateral
       requirements required herein associated with such transferred committed
       RBP UCAP MW obligation and, as applicable, the credit requirements in
       Tariff, Attachment Q. Transferee shall independently post sufficient RBP
       Collateral directly with the Office of the Interconnection to satisfy the
       incremental committed RBP UCAP MW associated with the acquired load.

             (2)    Transferor shall be released from its financial obligations for
       amount of RBP Collateral associated with the committed RBP UCAP MW
 associated with the transferred load. Any RBP Collateral posted by
transferor shall be returned once Transferee has posted the RBP Collateral
determined in accordance with Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.8(c) and
any unpaid invoice amounts associated with such transfer have been paid
by the transferor.

Attachment C




Affidavit of Gwen Kelly
                      UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                            BEFORE THE
              FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION


PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.                 )               Docket No. ER27-____-000


                     AFFIDAVIT OF GWEN KELLY
              ON BEHALF OF PJM INTERCONNECTION, L.L.C.

1.    My name is Gwen Kelly. I am the Senior Director, Credit Risk and Collateral
      Management at PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”). My business address is
      2750 Monroe Boulevard, Audubon, Pennsylvania 19403.

2.    I hold a Bachelor of Business Administration from the University of Hartford. I
      have more than 34 years of experience in credit and collateral management,
      including approximately 29 years in credit, treasury, and finance functions at
      subsidiaries of Public Service Enterprise Group, Inc. I have served in my current
      position at PJM since March 2021.

3.    In my current position, I am responsible for overseeing PJM’s credit risk
      management program, including the development and administration of collateral
      requirements and the evaluation of financial risks associated with participation in
      PJM-administered markets.

4.    The purpose of this affidavit is to explain and support PJM’s revised proposal for
      determining the credit requirements applicable to Load Serving Entities (“LSE”)
      allocated responsibility for charges associated with the Reliability Backstop
      Procurement (“RBP”). Specifically, I explain the credit risk considerations
      underlying the proposal, the economic analysis used to determine the proposed
      collateral level, and the manner in which the resulting credit requirements will be
      calculated and administered.

5.    I participated in the development and evaluation of the revised methodology. My
      statements are based on my experience in credit risk management, my
      responsibilities at PJM, and my review of the analyses underlying the proposal.

I.    Credit Risks Associated with Long-Term RBP Commitments

6.    The RBP provides for the procurement of capacity resources through commitments
      that may extend for up to 15 years. LSEs allocated responsibility for RBP Charges
      will have payment obligations associated with those commitments. The purpose of
      the buyer-side requirements is to mitigate the risk that an LSE will fail to satisfy
      those obligations, potentially resulting in unpaid amounts that may be allocated to
      other LSEs.
 7.    In developing the proposed credit methodology, PJM considered the long-term
      nature of RBP commitments. Although RBP Charges are calculated and settled
      periodically, the underlying procurement commitments extend over a substantially
      longer period. From a credit risk management perspective, PJM must establish
      appropriate protection against the financial exposure associated with those
      commitments over their terms.

8.    Assessing credit exposure over the term of an RBP commitment is not the same as
      estimating an LSE’s payment obligations for an individual Delivery Year. The
      periodic calculation of payment obligations does not necessarily mean that
      collateral requirements should be based primarily on expected payment exposure
      for each individual Delivery Year.

9.    Under the RBP settlement provisions, RBP Charges are calculated using a contract-
      for-differences mechanism. The RBP clearing price is established through the
      procurement process, but the Reliability Pricing Model (“RPM”) clearing prices
      used to calculate future settlement amounts are not known when the RBP
      commitments are established. Although RPM clearing prices affect RBP Charges,
      they are not inputs to PJM’s proposed calculation of the RBP LSE credit
      requirement.

10.   As a result, the actual RBP Charges payable over the commitment term may be
      substantially lower than the gross payment obligation calculated using the RBP
      clearing price. However, the amount of those future settlement obligations cannot
      be determined with certainty when the RBP commitments are established.

11.   One alternative approach to determining collateral requirements, which PJM is not
      proposing, would be to forecast future RPM clearing prices and use the estimated
      differences between those prices and the RBP clearing price to calculate expected
      payment exposure. Although such an approach could more closely reflect
      anticipated settlement obligations, it would depend on forecasts of RPM clearing
      prices extending many years into the future.

12.   Another approach would be to periodically adjust collateral requirements as future
      RPM clearing prices become known. Such adjustments could account for changes
      in expected payment exposure, but their effectiveness would depend on PJM’s
      ability to obtain additional collateral when needed.

13.   An increase in payment exposure may occur at a time when an LSE’s financial
      condition has deteriorated or when the LSE is otherwise unable to satisfy an
      additional collateral requirement. Under those circumstances, PJM could be left
      with insufficient collateral to secure the LSE’s payment obligations.

14.   Accordingly, PJM favors a methodology that establishes meaningful credit
      protection based on long-term RBP commitments rather than making that
      protection substantially dependent on forecasts of future RPM clearing prices or on
      the ability to obtain additional collateral over time.



                                           2
 15.    This does not mean that PJM assumes LSEs will ultimately pay the full gross value
       of their allocated RBP commitments, nor does it mean that collateral must equal the
       full gross value of those commitments. Instead, the RBP weighted-average clearing
       price provides a known and objectively determinable basis for calculating collateral
       requirements, while the appropriate level of collateral is determined through a
       separate economic analysis.

II.    Objective of the Revised LSE Credit Methodology

16.     PJM’s revised proposal is designed to establish a collateral requirement that
       balances the cost of providing collateral against the expected cost of socialized
       losses resulting from LSE payment defaults.

17.    In evaluating the appropriate amount of collateral, PJM considered two principal
       categories of costs. The first is the cost incurred by LSEs in posting the required
       collateral. The second is the expected cost of socialized default amounts that may
       be borne by non-defaulting LSEs if an LSE fails to satisfy its RBP payment
       obligations.

18.    These costs generally move in opposite directions as the amount of collateral
       changes. As the proportion of the gross RBP payment obligation secured by
       collateral increases, the cost of posting collateral increases, while the expected cost
       of socialized default amounts decreases.

19.    Accordingly, PJM sought to identify the collateral percentage at which the
       combined expected costs of posting collateral and socialized default amounts are
       minimized.

20.    This approach recognizes that requiring collateral equal to the entire gross RBP
       payment obligation would not necessarily produce the most economically
       reasonable result. Although additional collateral reduces the amount of unsecured
       exposure, it also imposes costs on the LSEs required to provide it.

21.    Similarly, a collateral requirement based primarily on minimizing the cost of
       posting collateral could result in insufficient protection against payment defaults,
       potentially leaving other LSEs to bear the resulting losses.

III.   Economic Analysis Supporting the Proposed Collateral Requirement

22.    To determine the appropriate collateral percentage, PJM performed an economic
       analysis evaluating the cost of posting collateral and the expected cost of socialized
       default amounts at different collateral levels, expressed as percentages of the net
       present value of the total RBP payment obligation.

23.    The principal inputs to this analysis include the weighted-average RBP clearing
       price, the credit quality of the LSE portfolio, the probability of default, the loss
       given default, and the cost of posting collateral.



                                             3
 24.      As noted in PJM’s July 31, 2026 transmittal letter and my supporting affidavit for
        that filing, PJM has used a discount rate of 9.5%, based on the capacity market
        Weighted Average Cost of Capital developed by The Brattle Group as part of PJM’s
        2025 periodic review of the Cost of New Entry of Capacity Resources into the PJM
        Region. PJM considers this rate appropriate for purposes of calculating the net
        present value of the total RBP payment obligation.1

        A.       Weighted-Average RBP Clearing Price

25.     The RBP clearing price is used to calculate the gross payment obligation that serves
        as the reference for determining collateral requirements. Because different RBP
        Resources may clear at different prices and have different quantities of committed
        capacity over their respective commitment terms, PJM proposes to use a weighted-
        average RBP clearing price.

26.     The weighted-average RBP clearing price is calculated by summing, for each RBP
        Seller and each Delivery Year of its commitment, the product of the applicable RBP
        clearing price and the committed RBP UCAP MW, and dividing that sum by the
        total RBP UCAP MW-years associated with those commitments.

27.     For purposes of the economic analysis and illustrative calculations, PJM assumed
        a weighted-average RBP clearing price of $555/MW-day. The actual RBP Credit
        Rate will be calculated using the weighted-average RBP clearing price determined
        from the procurement results rather than the illustrative $555/MW-day assumption.

        B.       LSE Credit Quality and Probability of Default

28.     PJM also considered the overall credit quality of the LSEs serving load in the PJM
        Region in developing its economic analysis. The weighted-average credit rating of
        this portfolio is BBB, which PJM used as an input to the analysis. A portfolio-level
        approach is appropriate because potential losses resulting from LSE payment
        defaults may be shared among non-defaulting LSEs, and the LSEs responsible for
        RBP payment obligations, as well as their credit quality, may change over the RBP
        commitment term, which can extend for up to 15 years. Accordingly, PJM’s
        methodology establishes a uniform collateral requirement based on the RBP
        obligations being secured rather than the individual credit ratings of the LSEs
        responsible for those obligations.

29.     The analysis uses the current LSE portfolio’s UCAP MW obligation weighted-
        average credit rating to determine the probability-of-default assumption. PJM used
        historical default information published by S&P Global in its Default, Transition,
        and Recovery: 2025 Annual U.S. Corporate Default and Rating Transition Study,
        particularly Table 11 (Average 10-Year Corporate Transition Rate (1981-
        2025)(%)), to inform that assumption. Based on this historical default information
1
 The Brattle Group, Brattle 2025 CONE Report for PJM, PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 26-34 (Apr. 9, 2025),
https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/committees-groups/committees/mic/2025/20250411-special/item-1-
02-revised-cone-report-final.pdf [https://perma.cc/B3VN-EY34].


                                                   4
       and the assumed portfolio credit rating of BBB, PJM’s economic analysis uses a
      probability-of-default assumption of 4.05%.

30.   Using a portfolio-wide credit rating assumption is consistent with PJM’s objective
      of establishing a uniform collateral methodology for LSEs assigned responsibility
      for RBP Charges. This does not mean that every LSE has a BBB credit rating or
      the same probability of default, but a uniform methodology is appropriate for the
      reasons discussed above.

      C.     Loss Given Default

31.   Another input is loss given default, which represents the percentage of the relevant
      payment exposure that PJM would not expect to recover following an LSE default.

32.   PJM’s economic analysis assumes a loss given default of 100% with respect to
      unsecured exposure, based on PJM’s historical experience with socialized losses
      resulting from LSE defaults. In those circumstances, PJM has generally not
      recovered amounts beyond the collateral available to secure the defaulting LSE’s
      obligations. Accordingly, the analysis assumes that any exposure remaining after
      application of available collateral would not be recovered following a default.

      D.     Cost of Posting Collateral

33.   The analysis also considers the cost incurred by LSEs in posting collateral.

34.   PJM’s analysis estimates the cost of posting collateral using a bank facility pricing
      approach based on the five-year historical trend in the 30-day average Secured
      Overnight Financing Rate (“SOFR”), plus an indicative credit spread associated
      with the assumed BBB credit rating of the LSE portfolio.

35.   PJM’s economic analysis uses an assumed cost-of-collateral rate of 4.93%,
      consisting     of       (a)       a      SOFR         rate       of      3.73%
      (https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/sofr); and (b) an indicative
      average BBB bank facility spread of 1.20%.

36.   To calculate the cost of posting collateral, PJM applied the assumed 4.93% annual
      cost of collateral to the gross RBP payment obligation associated with one MW of
      committed capacity over a 15-year term, multiplied by the applicable collateral
      percentage. PJM used a 40% collateral level because, as discussed below, its
      economic analysis identified that level as minimizing the combined cost of posting
      collateral and expected socialized default amounts. At that collateral level, using
      the illustrative weighted-average RBP clearing price of $555/MW-day, the
      calculated cost of posting collateral is approximately $59,962. This calculation is
      reflected as Point A in Figure 1 below.




                                           5
        E.       Cost of Socialized Default Amounts

37.    The cost of socialized default amounts represents the losses that may be borne by
       non-defaulting LSEs if an LSE fails to satisfy its RBP payment obligations. For
       illustrative purposes, PJM calculated the expected cost of socialized default
       amounts using the methodology shown in Table 1 below:

                       Table 1: Cost of Socialized Default Amounts

a) LSE Credit Ratings (weighted average)                             BBB
b) Probability of Default                                          4.05%
c) Loss Given Default                                               100%
                                                                         adjusted by the amount
d) expected default %                                              2.4% posted to PJM
e) Defaulted Amount                                              $73,839 =$555 x 1 x 365 x 15 x 2.4%
f) Collateral Held                                               $29,535 =$73,839 x 40%
g) Socialized Amount (=Defaulted Amount- Collateral Held)        $44,303 =$73,839 - $29,535
h) Socialized Cost to Non Default LSEs                           $45,407 =$44,303 / (1-2.4%)


38.    In Table 1:

       a)       LSE Credit Ratings represents the LSE portfolio’s UCAP MW obligation
                weighted-average credit rating.

       b)       Probability of Default is 4.05%, based on the historical 10-year corporate
                default rate for BBB rated entities reported by S&P Global.

       c)       Loss Given Default is assumed to be 100%, reflecting the assumption that
                PJM would not recover any unsecured losses from LSEs.

       d)       Expected default % represents the assumed probability of default after
                accounting for the effect of collateral posted to PJM. For purposes of its
                economic analysis, PJM assumes that the probability of default decreases
                proportionately as the percentage of the RBP payment obligation secured
                by collateral increases, from 4.05% with no collateral to zero with full
                collateralization. This simplifying assumption reflects PJM’s judgment that
                posting collateral can reduce the risk of default. At the proposed 40%
                collateral level, the resulting expected default percentage is approximately
                2.4%.

41.   PJM therefore proposes to use a 40% factor in determining the RBP Credit Rate.

42.   The 40% factor does not represent the percentage of gross RBP payments that PJM
      expects LSEs to pay through contract-for-differences settlements. Rather, it is the
      collateral percentage identified by PJM’s economic analysis as minimizing the
      combined cost of posting collateral and expected socialized default amounts.

IV.   Calculation of the RBP LSE Credit Requirement

43.   Under PJM’s proposed methodology, each LSE allocated responsibility for RBP
      Charges must maintain RBP Collateral sufficient to satisfy its RBP LSE credit
      requirement.

44.   Each LSE’s RBP LSE credit requirement is calculated by multiplying the RBP
      Credit Rate established following the applicable RBP auction by the LSE’s
      Allocated RBP Credit MW.

      RBP LSE Credit Requirement = RBP Credit Rate x Allocated RBP Credit MW

45.   The RBP Credit Rate is an amount per MW calculated by applying the 40% factor
      to the net present value of the total RBP payment obligation per MW over the
      applicable RBP commitment term, using the weighted-average RBP clearing price
      of all RBP UCAP MW committed through the RBP.




                                           9
 46.   Allocated RBP Credit MW means the RBP UCAP MW for which the LSE has been
      allocated responsibility for RBP Charges in accordance with the applicable Tariff
      provisions.

47.   The RBP Credit Rate therefore establishes a uniform dollar-per-MW amount based
      on the weighted-average RBP clearing price and the proposed collateral
      methodology. Each LSE’s total collateral requirement depends on the quantity of
      its Allocated RBP Credit MW.

48.   For example, at an assumed weighted-average RBP clearing price of $555/MW-
      day, the proposed methodology produces an illustrative RBP Credit Rate of
      approximately $686,000 per MW. This amount is equivalent to approximately 3.4
      years of undiscounted RBP payments per MW at the assumed clearing price.

49.   The approximately $686,000-per-MW amount is illustrative and does not represent
      a fixed RBP Credit Rate under the proposed Tariff provisions. The actual RBP
      Credit Rate will be calculated using the weighted-average RBP clearing price
      determined from the procurement results.

50.   The proposed methodology establishes the RPM Credit Rate by applying the 40%
      factor to the net present value of the total RBP payment obligation, rather than by
      requiring collateral equal to a specified number of years of payments.

V.    Administration of the RBP LSE Credit Requirement

      A.     Posting of Collateral

51.   The proposed Tariff provisions establish procedures for identifying the LSEs
      responsible for RBP Charges and requiring those LSEs to provide the applicable
      collateral before the beginning of each Delivery Year.

52.   Electric Distributors will provide PJM with the information necessary to identify
      the LSEs responsible for RBP Charges and their respective Allocated RBP Credit
      MW.

53.   LSEs responsible for RBP Charges must post or maintain the required RBP
      Collateral no later than 45 days before the beginning of the applicable Delivery
      Year.

54.   The annual identification and collateral posting process recognizes that
      responsibility for serving load, and consequently responsibility for RBP Charges,
      may change over the RBP commitment term. This annual process does not alter
      the long-term nature of the underlying RBP commitments or the long-term
      economic basis for determining the RBP Credit Rate.

55.   The proposed Tariff provisions also address circumstances in which an LSE is
      responsible for RBP Charges, but the information necessary to determine its
      Allocated RBP Credit MW has not been reported for the applicable Electric


                                          10
       Distributor zone or area. In those circumstances, PJM may determine the LSE’s
      Allocated RBP Credit MW using its proportional share of the Daily Unforced
      Capacity Obligation for the zone or area, as specified in the Tariff.

56.   In addition, the proposed Tariff provisions preserve PJM’s authority to evaluate an
      LSE under the Unreasonable Credit Risk provisions of Attachment Q.

      B.     Acceptable Forms of Collateral

57.   PJM proposes to accept RBP Collateral in the form of cash, letters of credit, or
      surety bonds, subject to PJM’s acceptance of the provider, form, and amount of
      such collateral. Consistent with PJM’s existing credit requirements, these forms of
      collateral are intended to provide reliable financial protection that PJM can access
      promptly when necessary, without conditions that could delay or impair its ability
      to obtain payment.

      C.     Relationship to Other PJM Credit Requirements

58.   The RBP LSE credit requirement addresses payment exposure associated with RBP
      commitments and is separate from the credit requirements applicable to other PJM
      market activities.

59.   PJM proposes that settlement during any Delivery Year of cleared positions
      resulting from, or expected to result from, the RBP, including payments and
      Locational Reliability Charges associated with the capacity commitments of RBP
      Resources, as well as RBP Charges, shall not be considered in Peak Market Activity
      under Tariff, Attachment Q, section VII.A. This treatment is intended to avoid
      duplicative collateral requirements for RBP-related exposure while preserving the
      application of other PJM credit requirements.

VI.   Review of the RBP Credit Rate

60.   Over the RBP commitment term, the inputs used to determine the RBP Credit Rate,
      including the overall credit quality of the LSE portfolio, may change.

61.   Following the commencement of commercial operation of all capacity resources
      with RBP commitments, PJM shall review the RBP Credit Rate, including inputs
      used to determine that rate.

62.   If PJM identifies material changes that would affect the RBP Credit Rate, PJM will
      reassess the RBP Credit Rate and present any resulting recommendations to PJM
      stakeholders through the Members Committee.

63.   A change in the credit characteristics of an individual LSE does not, by itself,
      trigger an adjustment to the RBP Credit Rate.

 VII.   Reasonableness of the Revised Methodology

64.    In my opinion, the revised RBP LSE credit methodology represents a reasonable
       approach to managing the financial risks associated with long-term RBP
       commitments.

65.    Using the known weighted-average RBP clearing price as the basis for determining
       collateral allows PJM to establish meaningful credit protection without relying on
       forecasts of future RPM clearing prices or on the ability to obtain additional
       collateral later in the commitment term.

66.    By considering both collateral costs and expected socialized default amounts, the
       methodology balances the interests of LSEs required to post collateral against those
       of LSEs that may bear losses resulting from another LSE’s payment default.

67.    Although alternative collateral methodologies are possible, including approaches
       based on projected contract-for-differences settlement exposure, PJM’s proposed
       methodology reflects a reasonable credit risk management judgment that balances
       the need for long-term credit protection against collateral costs and expected
       socialized default amounts.

VIII. Conclusion

68.    For the reasons explained above, I believe the proposed methodology represents a
       reasonable approach to establishing the RBP LSE credit requirement.
